answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Mirror Rule: each identity's action distribution in epoch N is compared against its own prior epochs via a fixed similarity test; large, unexplained divergence flags it. A flagged identity must complete a fresh voyage of onboarding epochs before regaining full weight. To spoof many identities, an attacker must sustain consistent behaviour per identity across epochs, and each operated identity needs its own bridge through the divergence check, multiplying operational cost per sybil.
